headline: FCC approves up to 1 million AI satellites for SpaceX
dek: According to CNBC, The Verge and SiliconANGLE, the Starmind constellation would be orbital data centers.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The approval
body: The FCC authorized SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites with AI chips (CNBC Technology, The Verge AI, SiliconANGLE).
The constellation is called Starmind and is described as orbital data centers.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How it would work
s3.body: According to SpaceX, power would come from the Sun.

points.t: Captures solar energy in space for AI tasks (The Verge AI).
Lasers tied to Starlink send data to Earth (The Verge AI).
Six altitude bands, according to SiliconANGLE.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Who objected
body: Amazon, Viasat and astronomers sought to block it, and the FCC rejected them (CNBC Technology, SiliconANGLE).
The agency says environmental and astronomy concerns fall outside its remit (CNBC Technology).

items.t: The full 1 million is due by 2040 (The Verge AI).
Missing a deadline voids the license, SiliconANGLE says.
Google and Blue Origin also eye space (CNBC Technology).

caption.hook: The FCC approved up to 1 million AI satellites for SpaceX.
body: The FCC authorized SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites with AI chips, according to CNBC, The Verge and SiliconANGLE. SpaceX describes the Starmind constellation as solar-powered data centers in orbit, with data sent to Earth by lasers tied to Starlink (The Verge AI).

Amazon, Viasat and astronomers tried to block the project, and the FCC rejected the petitions (CNBC Technology, SiliconANGLE). According to SiliconANGLE, missing any deadline voids the license, and the full 1 million is due by 2040. Google has already launched AI chips to space on a SpaceX rocket (CNBC Technology).
caption.cta: Are data centers in orbit a smart answer to AI's energy needs?
